judgements.justification: fBhF's (B) misstated improvement factor is a minor slip in praise, not a criticism; no score fell on a wrong claim.
B's AC gave no reading of its own; the spotlight is unexplained rather than argued above the scores, which R30 names.
B's mWXa gave the top score (8) on a four-sentence evaluation with no weakness, and B's meta-review cites only 'sufficient positive feedback'.
The authors disclosed nothing to one committee only; both ACs knew of the concurrent work.
Both ACs set the Makarychev and Shan overlap aside as independent work; the discounting is symmetric, not one committee's.
No score moved in either committee after the rebuttal.
Only A's reviewers raised the scoop by concurrent work, the 'artificial problem' framing and 'incremental' results; no B reviewer raised them.
Both ACs treated the concurrent work alike, as independent work needing a related-work update; no committee-level difference in weighting.
A's reviews were not split; the meta-review answers skXW's point but follows a uniform 7.0 mean.
No reviewer changed a score in either committee.
The authors answered every reviewer; gBnK's silence after the reply did not move a score.
B's mWXa 8 (four sentences, no discussion) and A's Hp5d 7 (three-sentence evaluation) counted unchallenged in the decisions.
Both committees accepted on positive majorities.
Neither AC stated a view and then deferred to a threshold.
No below-threshold score in either committee.
Both committees judged it as the same theory contribution on explainable clustering.
No reviewer raised a score on the rebuttal.
Both committees accepted the lack of experiments for a theory paper; no extra requirement held by one only.
No B reviewer's praise rests on a wrong claim about the paper; fBhF's factor slip did not drive the score.
fBhF kept his score after his concern was answered, but the score is 7, above threshold, not a held-down rating.
Both committees took the promised related-work comparison and conclusion on trust alike.
B's fBhF said he would give a strong accept but for missing experiments, then agreed experiments were not needed, without editing his 7; his raised stance is a main reason behind B's spotlight.
No off-record extra reviewer in either committee.
No clarity verdict split by reviewer expertise.
No rating was raised silently.
No detractor was set aside.
Each committee had one 8; A's 8 (skXW) argued that acceptance was a 'policy' question, not for the paper.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical school, beyond skXW calling the problem artificial.
B's meta-review argues only that reviewers gave 'sufficient positive feedback' for acceptance, yet the paper got a spotlight with no stated case at the same 7.0 mean as A.
A's skXW read the concurrent ICML papers and found bounds and algorithm very similar; no B reviewer mentioned them, so every B score treats the paper as the new state of the art.
Neither meta-review misstates reviewers' final positions.
skXW's 'artificial problem' concerns relevance to clustering practice, not audience breadth or venue fit, and A's AC did not cite it.
No misreading detractor in A; its lowest score (X5Zn, 6) is consistent with B's 6.
No new results were posted to one forum only.
A's expert skXW rated 8, but his text limited the case for a highlight; the non-expert scores did not set the tier against him.

reasoning: Both committees gave one 8, two 7s and one 6 (mean 7.0) and both ACs set the concurrent Makarychev and Shan work aside as independent, so the tier split rests on what the reviewers knew and on an unexplained AC choice. In A, skXW read the concurrent work and framed the paper as matched up to polylog factors (R31, R07). In B, no reviewer knew it, the top score was a thin four-sentence review (R03, R12), fBhF withdrew his one barrier to a strong accept without editing his score (R22), and the AC gave a spotlight with no stated case (R30). Existing reasons cover every cause; the candidate 'identical scores, tier left to AC' is R30, so no reason was added.
